memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. - Deut 6:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This single verse is the most treasured confession in all of Israel's faith. Devout Jews call it the Shema, from the Hebrew word for "hear," and they have recited it morning and evening for thousands of years. In a world crowded with countless gods and idols, this was a revolutionary declaration: there is one God, the Lord, and He alone is God. He is not one option among many, not a local deity for one nation among others. He is the one true and living God over all.

This truth changes everything. If there is only one God, then He alone deserves our whole worship, our full allegiance, our undivided hearts. We cannot serve Him alongside other loyalties. The oneness of God calls for the oneness of our devotion. Everything in life is meant to bend toward Him.

Remarkably, the New Testament does not overturn this confession but deepens it. Jesus Himself quoted the Shema as the greatest truth (Mark 12:29). And the early church, holding firmly to one God, came to know Him as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — one God in three Persons. When Jesus said "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30), He was including Himself in the very oneness of God. The Lord is one, and He has drawn near to us in Christ. To this one God belongs all our love and worship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is the Lord truly the one God of my life, or one loyalty among many?
- What competes with God for my undivided devotion?
- How does knowing there is one true God shape the way I live today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You alone are God, the one true and living God. Draw my divided heart together so that You have all my worship and allegiance. May everything in my life bend toward You. Amen.
